mainTopic: Lashes for a כהן גדול with an אלמנה, אביי and רבא on קידושין versus relations, and whether the daughter of a גר may marry a כהן
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier case: a כהן's forbidden act with a close relative makes her a זונה, and only a later act makes her a חללה. רב יהודה then rules that a כהן גדול with an אלמנה gets two sets of מלקות, for 'לא יקח' and 'לא יחלל'. The גמרא defends this against challenges from a משנה in מכות and shows that the ban on a חלוצה is only דרבנן. אביי and רבא then argue over whether קידושין alone brings lashes, and each agrees to an exception. Next, the גמרא brings a ברייתא proving רבי יהודה's view that the daughter of a male גר is unfit for כהונה. That proof combines the cases of a חלל, a כהן גדול with an אלמנה, and a first-generation מצרי through a הצד השוה argument. רבי שמעון בן יוחי allows a girl who converted before age three to marry a כהן. The גמרא then shows that all four views, the three in the משנה and רבי שמעון בן יוחי's in the ברייתא, come from different readings of one phrase in יחזקאל, 'מזרע בית ישראל'. The amud ends as רב נחמן begins to speak to רבא, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: First act makes her a זונה, a second act makes her a חללה
steps.stepSummary: Finishing an earlier case: the forbidden act makes the woman a זונה but not a חללה. If he has relations with her again, that second act makes her a חללה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He makes her a זונה, but he does not make her a חללה. If he comes back and has relations with her again, he makes her a חללה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a case from just before this section. It explains what status the woman gets after a first forbidden act and after a second one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first act makes her a זונה because the relationship was forbidden to him, but that prohibition is not a special כהונה rule, so it does not make her a חללה. Once she is a זונה, a כהן who has relations with her again breaks the כהונה prohibition of זונה, and that act makes her a חללה.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who had forbidden relations; she is forbidden to a כהן
A woman who lost the status allowing her to marry a כהן, through a relationship forbidden to כהונה
He makes her (into a certain status)
He came back and had relations with her again

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think זונה and חללה are the same thing. One act can make her a זונה without making her a חללה. The second status comes only from a later act that breaks a כהונה prohibition.

phrases.english: he renders her a zona,
phrases.notes: This finishes a case from just before: a כהן with a close relative forbidden to him.

phrases.english: he does not render her a chalala.
If he again engaged in intercourse with her,
he makes her a chalala.

steps.triggerLanguage: זוֹנָה מְשַׁוֵּי לַהּ, חֲלָלָה לָא מְשַׁוֵּי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes a discussion that began before this section
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A forbidden-relative act makes the woman a זונה, not a חללה. A later act by a כהן with her, now a זונה, makes her a חללה.

steps.title: A כהן גדול with a widow gets two sets of lashes
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rules that a כהן גדול who has relations with an אלמנה receives מלקות twice, once for 'לא יקח' and once for 'לא יחלל'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: A כהן גדול who has relations with a widow gets two sets of lashes. One is for 'he shall not take' and one is for 'he shall not profane'.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement begins. רב יהודה counts how many sets of lashes a כהן גדול gets for relations with a widow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two separate לאווים in the פסוקים. 'לא יקח' forbids taking her, and 'לא יחלל' forbids profaning her, which the act does by making her a חללה. Because these are two prohibitions, one act brings two sets of lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: The High Priest
A widow, forbidden to the כהן גדול
He is flogged; he receives מלקות
'He shall not take': the prohibition against taking her
'He shall not profane': the prohibition against profaning

steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling is the claim that the rest of this section questions and defends.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda says:
A High Priest who has relations with a widow
is flogged two sets of lashes,
one due to "He shall not take,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:14

phrases.english: and one due to "He shall not profane."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:15

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל בְּאַלְמָנָה לוֹקֶה שְׁתַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, connected to the theme of making a woman a חללה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן גדול with an אלמנה gets two sets of מלקות: 'לא יקח' and 'לא יחלל'.

steps.title: Why not a third set for profaning his offspring?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why he does not also get lashes for 'לא יחלל זרעו', since a child from this act would be a חלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he should also be flogged because of 'he shall not profane his offspring'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב יהודה's count of two. The full פסוק also speaks about his offspring, so maybe there should be a third set of lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'לא יחלל זרעו', 'he shall not profane his offspring'. A child born from this union is a חלל, so the act seems to break that part too. So why does רב יהודה stop at two?

keyTerms.meaning: And let him also be flogged
His offspring

phrases.english: But let him also be flogged
due to "He shall not profane his offspring"!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִילְקֵי נָמֵי מִשּׁוּם לֹא יְחַלֵּל זַרְעוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the number of lashes in רב יהודה's ruling
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's count of only two sets of lashes
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק also forbids profaning offspring, and this act produces a חלל, so there should be a third set.

steps.title: The case is where he did not complete the act
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that רב יהודה speaks of a case where the act was not completed, so no offspring can result.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about a case where he did not finish his act of relations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב יהודה by narrowing the case he is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An incomplete act cannot produce a child, so 'לא יחלל זרעו' does not apply. The other two prohibitions still apply, which is why רב יהודה says two.

keyTerms.meaning: Completed his act of relations

phrases.english: Where he did not complete his intercourse.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּשֶׁלֹּא גָּמַר בִּיאָתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 3
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every case of a כהן גדול with a widow would include profaning offspring, so there should be three sets of lashes.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב יהודה means an incomplete act, so only two prohibitions apply.

steps.title: רבא challenges from a משנה about 'two labels'
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a משנה that says a man who has relations with a woman who is both a widow and a divorcée is flogged for 'two labels'. That seems to mean only two sets of lashes in total.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא objected: A widow who is also a divorcée, he is flogged for two labels. Doesn't that mean two labels and no more?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רב יהודה using a משנה. He reads it as saying there are only two sets of lashes in total.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'widow' alone already brings two sets, as רב יהודה says, then widow plus divorcée should bring four. The משנה says only 'two labels', which suggests one set per prohibition. That would go against רב יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: He raises an objection from an earlier source
A divorcée, forbidden to every כהן
Two labels, meaning two named prohibitions
Is it not that...? (a lead-in to a forced reading)
And no more

phrases.english: Rava raises an objection:
A widow who is also a divorcée:
he is flogged due to two labels.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי לָאו שְׁנֵי שֵׁמוֹת וְתוּ לָא?
phrases.english: Is it not two labels and no more?

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵתִיב רָבָא: אַלְמָנָה וּגְרוּשָׁה לוֹקֶה מִשּׁוּם שְׁנֵי שֵׁמוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After steps 3-4, goes back to attack רב יהודה's basic ruling from a משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's ruling of two sets of lashes for a widow alone
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה gives only two labels for widow plus divorcée. That suggests one set each, not two per prohibition.

steps.title: Two labels for each woman-type
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה means two labels for the widow and two labels for the divorcée.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It means two labels for this one and two labels for that one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects רבא's reading of the משנה, so רב יהודה is not contradicted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Two labels' is read as applying to each prohibition separately. For each one there is 'לא יקח' and 'לא יחלל'. So the משנה fits רב יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: For this one

steps.whatToRemember: רב יהודה stands: a כהן גדול with an אלמנה gets two sets of lashes, 'לא יקח' and 'לא יחלל'. There is no third set for 'זרעו' when the act is not completed. The משנה's 'two labels' means two for each prohibition.

phrases.english: No; two labels for this one
and two labels for that one.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, שְׁנֵי שֵׁמוֹת עַל זֶה וּשְׁנֵי שֵׁמוֹת עַל זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's objection by rereading the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Two labels' means two sets of lashes in total.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Two labels' means two for the widow and two for the divorcée, which fits רב יהודה.

steps.title: The last clause of the משנה says only one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the reading from step 6 using the סיפא of the same משנה: a גרושה who is also a חלוצה brings lashes for only one.
steps.simpleTranslation: If that is how you read the משנה, look at its last clause: 'A divorcée who is also a חלוצה: he is liable for only one!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 6 by quoting the next line of the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a גרושה brings two labels ('לא יקח' and 'לא יחלל'), as רב יהודה says, then a גרושה וחלוצה should also bring at least two. But the סיפא says he is liable for only one. That seems to show a גרושה brings only one set of lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, if that is the case
The latter clause of a משנה or ברייתא
A widow released from יבום by חליצה
A divorced woman, forbidden to a כהן

phrases.english: If so, say the latter clause:
A divorcée who is also a חלוצה:
he is liable for only one!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי אֵימָא סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the step 6 reading of 'two labels' using the next clause of the same משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 6's claim that the משנה counts two labels for each forbidden category, which supports רב יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a גרושה alone brings two labels, the סיפא could not say 'only one' for a גרושה וחלוצה

steps.title: Only one forbidden category, but still two labels
steps.stepSummary: The 'one' in the סיפא means one category (the divorce counts and the חליצה does not), but that one category still brings two labels.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: he is liable only for one thing, being a divorcée, but that one thing really brings two labels.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'only one' counts forbidden categories, not sets of lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the divorce brings lashes, because the חליצה part is not a Torah ban (step 10 explains this). That single category of גרושה still brings two sets of lashes, 'לא יקח' and 'לא יחלל'. So רב יהודה still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means (the גמרא reinterprets the wording)
But really, in truth
Two labels, two separate prohibitions

steps.confusionAlert: 'Only one' here does NOT mean one set of lashes. It means one forbidden category, the divorce, which by itself brings two sets of lashes.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
he is liable for only one,
but really, two labels.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 7 by reinterpreting 'one'
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Only one' means only one set of lashes
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Only one' means one forbidden category (גרושה), which still brings two labels

steps.title: Isn't the ban on a חלוצה from the Torah?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how a חלוצה can be only דרבנן, when a ברייתא learns her ban from the word 'ואשה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is a חלוצה only forbidden by the רבנן? But a ברייתא teaches: 'Divorcée': this only teaches a divorcée; where do we learn a חלוצה? The verse says 'and a woman'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea behind step 8, that the ban on a חלוצה is only rabbinic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 only works if the חלוצה part adds no Torah lashes. A ברייתא seems to learn from the extra 'ו' in 'ואשה' that a חלוצה counts as a kind of divorcée. If that is a Torah law, she should add lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: From the Rabbis, not from the Torah
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא?
From where do we learn it?
The verse teaches

phrases.english: And is a חלוצה only rabbinic?
But isn't it taught:
'Divorcée': I have only a divorcée;
from where do we learn a חלוצה?
The verse says: 'And a woman'!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:7. The extra 'and' is read as adding the חלוצה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲלוּצָה דְּרַבָּנַן? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the assumption behind step 8, that a חלוצה is forbidden only by the רבנן
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that the ban on a חלוצה to a כהן is rabbinic
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא derives the ban on a חלוצה from a פסוק, so it seems to be a Torah law

steps.title: The verse is only a support for a rabbinic law
steps.stepSummary: The ban on a חלוצה really is דרבנן, and the פסוק in the ברייתא is only an אסמכתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is from the רבנן, and the verse is just a support.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא's verse is only a hint the רבנן attached to their own law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אסמכתא is a פסוק used to support a rabbinic rule, not its real source. So the ban on a חלוצה brings no Torah lashes, and the reading in step 8 holds.

keyTerms.meaning: A mere support: a verse attached to a rabbinic law, not its real source
The verse

steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches a common pattern in ש״ס: a ברייתא can cite a פסוק even for a law that is only rabbinic.

phrases.english: It is rabbinic,
and the verse is a mere support.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּרַבָּנַן, וּקְרָא אַסְמַכְתָּא בְּעָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9 by downgrading the verse to an אסמכתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's verse makes the ban on a חלוצה a Torah law
steps.terutzMaskana: The ban on a חלוצה is rabbinic, and the verse only supports it

steps.title: אביי: lashes for betrothal and lashes for relations
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules that a כהן who does קידושין with a forbidden woman gets lashes for 'לא יקח', and if he has relations he gets more lashes for 'לא יחלל'.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: If he betrothed her, he is flogged. If he had relations with her, he is flogged. For betrothing, because of 'he shall not take'. For relations, because of 'he shall not profane'.
steps.whatsHappening: A new discussion begins. אביי explains which act brings which set of lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי matches each לאו to a different act. Taking (קידושין) breaks 'לא יקח' even without relations. Relations (ביאה) breaks 'לא יחלל'.

keyTerms.meaning: He betrothed (did קידושין)
He had relations
He is flogged, receives מלקות
'He shall not take': the ban on marrying her
'He shall not profane': the ban tied to the act of relations

phrases.english: אביי said:
If he betrothed, he is flogged; if he had relations, he is flogged.
If he betrothed, he is flogged because of 'he shall not take'.
If he had relations, he is flogged because of 'he shall not profane'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: קִידֵּשׁ – לוֹקֶה, בָּעַל – לוֹקֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question: which act triggers each of רב יהודה's two לאוין
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קידושין alone brings lashes for 'לא יקח', and relations bring lashes for 'לא יחלל'

steps.title: רבא: no lashes without relations
steps.stepSummary: רבא disagrees: without relations there are no lashes, because 'לא יקח' exists only so that he will not come to 'לא יחלל'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If he had relations, he is flogged. If he did not, he is not flogged, because it is written 'he shall not take... and he shall not profane'. Why 'not take'? So that he not profane.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the opposite view to אביי's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא reads the two phrases as connected. The ban on taking is there to prevent the profaning act. So קידושין alone, with no relations, brings no lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is written
For what reason?

steps.whatToRemember: אביי: קידושין alone brings lashes ('לא יקח'). רבא: only relations bring lashes, because 'לא יקח' serves 'לא יחלל'.

phrases.english: רבא said:

phrases.aramaic: בָּעַל – לוֹקֶה, לֹא בָּעַל – אֵינוֹ לוֹקֶה,
phrases.english: If he had relations, he is flogged; if he did not, he is not flogged,
because it is written: 'He shall not take... and he shall not profane'
Why 'he shall not take'?
Because of 'he shall not profane'.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: בָּעַל – לוֹקֶה, לֹא בָּעַל – אֵינוֹ לוֹקֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposing view to אביי's ruling
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only relations bring lashes, because 'לא יקח' exists to prevent 'לא יחלל'

steps.title: אביי agrees about remarrying a divorced wife
steps.stepSummary: Even אביי admits that a man who remarries his divorced wife gets no lashes for קידושין alone, because the פסוק speaks of taking her 'to be his wife'.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי agrees about one who remarries his divorced wife: if he betrothed her but did not have relations, he is not flogged. The Torah says 'to take her to be his wife', and that is missing here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a limit to אביי's view: in one case even he agrees with רבא's result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For מחזיר גרושתו the פסוק says 'to be his wife', which points to married life together. Betrothal without relations does not reach that, so even אביי gives no lashes there. This is an exception in how the law works, built on that פסוק's wording.

keyTerms.meaning: Agrees, concedes
Remarrying one's divorced wife after she married someone else
The Merciful One, the Torah
It is not there, it is missing

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that אביי's rule depends on the wording of each לאו. Where the פסוק stresses being a wife, קידושין alone is not enough.

phrases.english: And אביי agrees about one who remarries his divorced wife,
phrases.notes: This is any Jew, not just a כהן: he remarries his ex-wife after she married someone else.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאִם קִידֵּשׁ וְלֹא בָּעַל – שֶׁאֵינוֹ לוֹקֶה.
phrases.english: that if he betrothed and did not have relations, he is not flogged.
'To take her to be his wife', the Merciful One said,
phrases.notes: דברים 24:4

phrases.english: and that is not present here.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמוֹדֶה אַבָּיֵי בְּמַחֲזִיר גְּרוּשָׁתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits אביי's ruling from step 11 with an exception case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For מחזיר גרושתו, קידושין without relations brings no lashes even according to אביי, since the פסוק requires 'to be his wife'

steps.title: רבא agrees: relations without קידושין bring lashes for a כהן גדול with a widow
steps.stepSummary: רבא admits that a כהן גדול who has relations with an אלמנה without קידושין gets lashes for 'לא יחלל', because by the act of relations he has profaned her.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא agrees about a כהן גדול with a widow: if he had relations without doing קידושין, he gets lashes. The Torah says 'He shall not profane his offspring among his people,' and he has profaned her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the other side of the argument. Even רבא, who said קידושין alone brings no lashes, agrees that relations alone do bring lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said that 'לא יקח' only exists to protect against 'לא יחלל'. So when the act of 'לא יחלל' really happens through relations, even without קידושין, it is a full לאו with lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: Agrees; admits to a point
The High Priest
A widow, forbidden to a כהן גדול
He had relations but did not do קידושין

phrases.english: And רבא agrees about a כהן גדול with a widow,
that if he had relations without קידושין, he gets lashes.
The Merciful One said: 'And he shall not profane his offspring among his people,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:15

phrases.english: and look, he has profaned [her].

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמוֹדֶה רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 13: there אביי gave in on one point, and here רבא gives in on another.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Relations alone, without קידושין, between a כהן גדול and an אלמנה bring lashes for 'לא יחלל'.

steps.title: Both agree: no lashes for relations alone with a divorced wife
steps.stepSummary: אביי and רבא both agree that a man who has relations with his divorced wife without קידושין gets no lashes, because the Torah only forbade 'taking' her.
steps.simpleTranslation: And both agree about a man who takes back his divorced wife: if he had relations without doing קידושין, he does not get lashes. The Torah only forbade the way of 'taking', meaning marriage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the topic with a point both אביי and רבא accept, about remarrying a divorced wife after she was married to someone else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The לאו here is worded as 'taking her to be his wife', which means marriage. Relations without קידושין are not marriage, so this לאו is not broken. This is different from the כהן גדול case, where 'לא יחלל' is broken by the act itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Both of them agree
A man who takes back his divorced wife after she married someone else
By way of 'taking', meaning marriage

steps.whatToRemember: Relations alone with an אלמנה: lashes for a כהן גדול, because the act itself profanes her ('לא יחלל'). Relations alone with his divorced wife: no lashes, because only marriage is forbidden.

phrases.english: And both agree about one who takes back his divorced wife,
phrases.notes: This means after she married someone else (דברים 24:4), and 'both' means אביי and רבא.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאִם בָּעַל וְלֹא קִידֵּשׁ – שֶׁאֵינוֹ לוֹקֶה,
phrases.english: that if he had relations without קידושין, he does not get lashes,
since the Torah forbade it only by way of taking (marriage).

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁנֵיהֶם מוֹדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a point both sides accept, which closes the אביי and רבא discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No lashes for relations alone with a divorced wife who remarried, since the לאו is only against marriage.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: the daughter of a male convert is like the daughter of a חלל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה's view from the משנה and brings a ברייתא with the same words.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: The daughter of a male גר is like the daughter of a חלל. It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יהודה says the daughter of a male גר is like the daughter of a male חלל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting רבי יהודה from the משנה. It then brings the ברייתא that will try to prove his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The daughter of a male חלל may not marry a כהן. רבי יהודה says the daughter of a male גר has the same rule. The ברייתא repeats this so it can bring a proof next.

keyTerms.meaning: The daughter of a male convert
A son born from a forbidden כהונה union, who lost the status of כהונה
It was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: רבי יהודה says:
The daughter of a male convert is like the daughter of a חלל.
phrases.notes: This is quoted from our משנה. It means she may not marry a כהן.

phrases.english: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יהודה says:

phrases.aramaic: בַּת גֵּר זָכָר כְּבַת חָלָל זָכָר.
phrases.english: The daughter of a male convert is like the daughter of a male חלל.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: בַּת גֵּר זָכָר כְּבַת חָלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic, going back to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, the daughter of a male גר may not marry a כהן.

steps.title: A קל וחומר from a חלל to a convert
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא argues that if a חלל, who comes from Jewish parents, has an unfit daughter, then surely a גר, who comes from non-Jewish parents, has an unfit daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: And logic says so too. A חלל comes from a fit drop of seed, and still his daughter is unfit. A גר comes from an unfit drop of seed. Isn't it logical that his daughter is unfit?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a logical proof, a קל וחומר, for רבי יהודה's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חלל has two Jewish parents, so his origin is 'fit', and still his daughter is unfit. A גר was born to non-Jews, so his origin is 'unfit'. If the better case has an unfit daughter, the weaker case surely does too.

keyTerms.meaning: And logic says so too
A fit drop of seed, meaning a Jewish father
An unfit drop of seed, meaning a non-Jewish father
Isn't it logical? This is how a קל וחומר is introduced

phrases.english: And logic says so too:
Just as a חלל, who comes from a fit drop,
phrases.notes: 'Fit drop' means his parents were both Jewish.

phrases.english: has an unfit daughter,
a convert, who comes from an unfit drop,
isn't it logical that his daughter is unfit?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַדִּין נוֹתֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the logical source for the rule quoted in step 16.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה's rule that the daughter of a male גר is unfit for כהונה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from the daughter of a חלל

steps.title: A חלל is different because he was formed through a sin
steps.stepSummary: The proof is challenged: a חלל was conceived through a forbidden act, but a גר was not, so the two cases cannot be compared.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about a חלל? He is different, because he was formed through a sin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the קל וחומר by pointing out something stricter about a חלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חלל was born from a forbidden union. The non-Jewish parents of a גר did nothing forbidden. So maybe the sin is why a חלל's daughter is unfit, and that reason would not apply to a גר.

keyTerms.meaning: What about...? This is how the גמרא shows the source case is special
He was formed (conceived) through a sin

phrases.english: What about a חלל?
He is different, because he was formed through a sin.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְחָלָל, שֶׁכֵּן יְצִירָתוֹ בַּעֲבֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the קל וחומר from step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison between a חלל and a גר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The source case has a stricter feature, being conceived in sin, that the גר lacks.

steps.title: A כהן גדול with a widow proves the sin is not the reason
steps.stepSummary: A כהן גדול who has a daughter with an אלמנה was not himself conceived in sin, yet his daughter is unfit, so the sin of conception is not the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: A כהן גדול with a widow will prove it: he was not formed through a sin, and still his daughter is unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by bringing a different case where the daughter is unfit even without the father being conceived in sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהן גדול himself was born in a proper way. Still, a daughter he has from a widow is a חללה. So 'being conceived in sin' is not needed for a daughter to be unfit.

keyTerms.meaning: Will prove it; a case that shows the rule holds without that feature

phrases.english: A כהן גדול with a widow will prove it,
since he was not formed through a sin,
and still his daughter is unfit.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל בְּאַלְמָנָה יוֹכִיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18 by bringing a new source case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a different source case that does not have the challenged feature
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe a daughter is unfit only because her father was conceived in sin.
steps.terutzMaskana: A כהן גדול with a widow shows a daughter can be unfit without that.

steps.title: A כהן גדול with a widow is different because his relations are a sin
steps.stepSummary: The new source case is challenged: the כהן גדול's relations with the widow are themselves forbidden, which a גר's relations are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about a כהן גדול with a widow? He is different, because his relations are a sin!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new proof by pointing out something strict about the כהן גדול case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהן גדול breaks a לאו when he lives with the widow. A גר who marries a Jewish woman does nothing forbidden. So maybe the forbidden relations are why the daughter is unfit.

keyTerms.meaning: His relations are a sin

phrases.english: What about a כהן גדול with a widow?
He is different, because his relations are a sin!

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל בְּאַלְמָנָה, שֶׁכֵּן בִּיאָתוֹ בַּעֲבֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source case brought in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using the כהן גדול with a widow as a source
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This source case has its own strict feature, forbidden relations, that a גר lacks.

steps.title: A חלל proves the forbidden relations are not the reason
steps.stepSummary: A חלל who marries a Jewish woman does nothing forbidden, yet his daughter is unfit, so forbidden relations are not the reason either.
steps.simpleTranslation: A חלל will prove it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the first case, the חלל, to answer the challenge to the second case. This sets up a combined proof from both cases together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חלל's own relations with a Jewish woman are allowed, and still his daughter is unfit. So each case answers the challenge against the other. The argument now goes back and forth between the two cases, which prepares the ground for proving the rule from what they share.

keyTerms.meaning: A חלל will prove it

steps.confusionAlert: 'His daughter' in step 19 means the daughter of the כהן גדול from the widow. Here the point is that a חלל's own relations are allowed, but his daughter is still unfit.
steps.whyThisMatters: Each case blocks the challenge against the other. This is the classic pattern that leads to learning from what the two cases have in common.

phrases.english: A חלל will prove it.
phrases.notes: A חלל may marry a regular Jewish woman, so his relations are no sin, yet his daughter is still unfit.

steps.triggerLanguage: חָלָל יוֹכִיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 20 by going back to the חלל case from step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Goes back to the first source case, which does not have the challenged feature
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe a daughter is unfit only because her father's relations were forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: A חלל's relations are allowed, yet his daughter is unfit, so that feature is not needed.

steps.title: Combining the two cases: what they share
steps.stepSummary: Since neither חלל nor כהן גדול with an אלמנה works alone, the ברייתא combines them. Their shared feature is that they are 'not like most of the congregation,' and a גר shares that feature too, so his daughter is unfit.
steps.simpleTranslation: The argument has come back around. Each case has its own weakness, but what they have in common is that they are not like most of the congregation. So I will bring the גר, who is also not like most of the congregation, and say his daughter is unfit too.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא builds a new proof from both earlier cases together. It looks for what they share and applies that to a גר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each case alone had a weakness: the חלל was conceived in sin, and the כהן גדול sinned in the act itself. A הצד השוה argument ignores each case's weakness and uses only what both cases share. Here that is being different from ordinary Jews, which a גר also is.

keyTerms.meaning: The argument goes back around: we return to the earlier cases and use them together
The feature of this one is not like the feature of that one: each case is special in its own way
The shared feature: proving a law from what two sources have in common
Most of the congregation: ordinary Jews of normal lineage
His daughter is unfit to marry a כהן

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic example of the הצד השוה method. Two weak proofs are combined into one stronger proof.

phrases.english: And the argument has come back around
phrases.notes: Each case alone was knocked down, so now we go back and use both cases from Steps 17–21 together.

phrases.english: the feature of this one is not like the feature of that one
the feature they share
is that they are not like most of the congregation
so I too will bring the convert
who is not like most of the congregation
and his daughter is unfit.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחָזַר הַדִּין, לֹא רְאִי זֶה כִּרְאִי זֶה, הַצַּד הַשָּׁוֶה שֶׁבָּהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on Step 21: each case has a weakness the other answers, so the ברייתא combines them through הצד השוה.
steps.raayaObject: That a גר's daughter is unfit to marry a כהן
steps.raayaSupportSource: The shared feature of חלל and כהן גדול with an אלמנה: both are not like most of the congregation

steps.title: Both cases involve some sin
steps.stepSummary: The shared-feature proof is challenged. Both חלל and כהן גדול with an אלמנה involve some sin, either in how the person was conceived or in the act itself, and a גר involves none.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about their shared feature? It is special because both cases have some element of sin in them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the combined proof. It points to a second shared feature, sin, that a גר does not have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A הצד השוה proof can be broken if the two sources share another feature the new case lacks. Here both sources involve sin: the חלל was conceived through sin, and the כהן גדול commits a sin. Maybe the sin is what makes the daughter unfit, so a גר cannot be compared.

keyTerms.meaning: What about the shared feature? The standard way to attack a הצד השוה proof
An element of sin

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the same objection as Steps 18 and 20. There each case was attacked alone. Here the point is that both cases share the element of sin, so even together they fail.

phrases.english: What about the feature they share?
It is that they have an element of sin in them!
phrases.notes: For the חלל the sin was in how he was conceived. For the כהן גדול the sin is the forbidden relations themselves.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְהַצַּד הַשָּׁוֶה שֶׁבָּהֶן, שֶׁכֵּן יֵשׁ בָּהֶם צַד עֲבֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the הצד השוה proof of Step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The combined proof from חלל and כהן גדול with an אלמנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both sources share an element of sin that a גר lacks, so the sin, not being 'unlike the congregation,' may be the real reason.

steps.title: Use a first-generation Egyptian convert instead
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא swaps out the כהן גדול with an אלמנה for a first-generation מצרי convert. His marriage to an Egyptian convert woman involves no sin, yet their daughter is still unfit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Don't say a כהן גדול with a widow proves it. Say instead that a first-generation Egyptian convert proves it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repairs the proof by replacing one of the two source cases. The new case has no sin at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the pair is חלל and מצרי ראשון. A first-generation מצרי who marries a first-generation מצרית does nothing forbidden, yet their offspring are unfit for כהונה. So the shared feature of the new pair no longer includes sin, which removes the objection of Step 23.

keyTerms.meaning: Don't say this, rather say that: replacing one case or wording with another
A first-generation Egyptian convert. Egyptians may enter the קהל only from the third generation.

phrases.aramaic: לָא תֵּימָא כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל בְּאַלְמָנָה יוֹכִיחַ,
phrases.english: Don't say that a High Priest with a widow will prove it
rather say: a first-generation Egyptian will prove it.
phrases.notes: He means a first-generation Egyptian convert married to a first-generation Egyptian convert woman. Their marriage is allowed, yet their children are unfit for כהונה.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא תֵּימָא כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל בְּאַלְמָנָה יוֹכִיחַ, אֶלָּא אֵימָא: מִצְרִי רִאשׁוֹן יוֹכִיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 23 by replacing the source case that involved sin.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The daughter is unfit only because of some element of sin.
steps.terutzMaskana: A מצרי ראשון involves no sin, yet his offspring are unfit, so sin is not required.

steps.title: An Egyptian convert cannot enter the congregation
steps.stepSummary: The new case is challenged. A first-generation מצרי is not allowed to enter the קהל at all, while a גר is, so the cases cannot be compared.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about a first-generation Egyptian? He is special because he is not fit to enter the congregation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the replacement case. It points to a feature of the מצרי ראשון that a גר does not have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מצרי ראשון may not marry a born Jewish woman, but an ordinary גר may. Maybe that more serious flaw is why his offspring are unfit for כהונה. If so, he does not prove anything about a regular גר.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, or because: introduces the special feature that blocks the comparison
He is not fit to enter the congregation, meaning he may not marry a born Jewish woman

phrases.english: What about a first-generation Egyptian?
He is special because he is not fit to enter the congregation.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְמִצְרִי רִאשׁוֹן, שֶׁכֵּן אֵינוֹ רָאוּי לָבֹא בַּקָּהָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the substitute case introduced in Step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: The מצרי ראשון as a source case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A מצרי ראשון is barred from the קהל entirely, unlike a גר. That flaw may be the reason his offspring are unfit.

steps.title: A חלל proves that point does not matter
steps.stepSummary: A חלל may enter the קהל and marry a Jewish woman, yet his daughter is unfit. So being barred from the קהל is not the reason the daughter is unfit.
steps.simpleTranslation: A חלל will prove it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the challenge by pointing back to the other source case, the חלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each source in the pair now covers the other's weakness. The מצרי ראשון involves no sin, and the חלל is allowed in the קהל. Since both have unfit daughters, the real shared reason is being 'unlike most of the congregation,' and that applies to a גר too.

keyTerms.meaning: A son of a כהן from a marriage forbidden to a כהן. He loses כהונה but may marry a regular Jewish woman.
Will prove it: points to a case that disproves the objection

steps.whatToRemember: The final pair is חלל and מצרי ראשון. Neither one's weakness is shared by the other, so the next step builds a common-feature proof from them. Step 28 challenges that proof, and step 29 upholds it according to רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: A חלל will prove it.
phrases.notes: A חלל is allowed to marry a regular Jewish woman, yet his daughter still cannot marry a כהן.

steps.triggerLanguage: חָלָל יוֹכִיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 25 by using the other source case, the חלל.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The other source case answers the objection (הצד השוה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The offspring are unfit only because the father is barred from the קהל.
steps.terutzMaskana: A חלל may enter the קהל, yet his daughter is unfit, so being barred is not the reason.

steps.title: Combining the חלל and the מצרי into one proof
steps.stepSummary: Neither the חלל nor the first-generation מצרי works alone as a source. Their shared feature is that they are not like most of the קהל, and their daughters are unfit. A גר shares that feature, so his daughter is unfit too.
steps.simpleTranslation: The argument has come back to where it started. These two cases are not the same, but they share one thing: neither is like most of the congregation, and the daughter of each is unfit. So I will add the convert, who is also not like most of the congregation, and his daughter is unfit too.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the מצרי has replaced the כהן גדול with an אלמנה, the גמרא runs the common-feature proof again with this new pair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each case alone can be challenged. A חלל comes from a sinful union, and a מצרי is barred from the קהל. But both share one thing: they are not like most of the קהל, and their daughters are unfit. A גר is also not like most of the קהל, so the same law should apply to his daughter.

keyTerms.meaning: The argument has come back to its starting point.
This case is not like that case. Each one has its own weakness.
The common feature that two cases share.
Most of the Jewish congregation, meaning ordinary Jews with no flaw in their lineage.

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the final form of רבי יהודה's proof. The next steps test whether the shared feature really covers the גר.

phrases.english: And the argument has gone back to the start.
phrases.notes: Neither case worked alone, so the גמרא goes back to combining two cases. This time the pair is the חלל and the מצרי.

phrases.english: The aspect of this one is not like the aspect of that one,

phrases.aramaic: הַצַּד הַשָּׁוֶה שֶׁבָּהֶן – שֶׁאֵינָן בְּרוֹב קָהָל,
phrases.english: but the common feature between them is that they are not like most of the congregation,
and his daughter is unfit.
So I too will bring in the convert,
who is not like most of the congregation, and his daughter is unfit.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחָזַר הַדִּין. לֹא רְאִי זֶה כִּרְאִי זֶה, הַצַּד הַשָּׁוֶה שֶׁבָּהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 26 showed the מצרי still works as a source. Now the גמרא pairs it with the חלל and rebuilds the common-feature proof.
steps.raayaObject: The daughter of a גר is unfit to marry a כהן (רבי יהודה).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The shared feature of a חלל and a first-generation מצרי: not like most of the קהל, and their daughters are unfit.

steps.title: The shared feature is that they disqualify through relations
steps.stepSummary: The proof is challenged. The חלל and the מצרי share a stronger feature: when they have relations with a woman, she becomes unfit for a כהן. A גר does not seem to share that.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about their common feature? These two disqualify a woman through their relations, so they are different from a convert.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the common-feature proof by pointing to a different shared feature that the גר does not have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חלל and a מצרי both make a woman unfit for כהונה when they have relations with her. That is a stronger kind of flaw than just being 'not like most of the קהל.' Since a גר seems to lack this flaw, the proof should not reach him.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What about...?' The standard way to point out a difference that breaks a comparison.
They make a woman unfit for a כהן by having relations with her.

phrases.english: What about the common feature between them?
They are different, since they disqualify a woman through their relations.
phrases.notes: He means a woman who lives with one of them becomes unfit to marry a כהן. A גר is assumed not to do this.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְהַצַּד הַשָּׁוֶה שֶׁבָּהֶן, שֶׁכֵּן פּוֹסְלִים בְּבִיאָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the common-feature proof built in step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: The common-feature proof from the חלל and the מצרי to the גר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The two sources share a stricter feature, disqualifying a woman through relations, which a גר lacks. So the proof cannot carry over to him.

steps.title: For רבי יהודה, a גר also disqualifies through relations
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה holds that a גר also makes a woman unfit through relations. So for him the גר shares even that feature, and he derives the daughter's law from the common feature of the חלל and the מצרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה? He holds that a convert also disqualifies a woman through his relations. So he derives this law through a 'common feature' argument from these cases.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. In רבי יהודה's own view, the גר does share the feature that was raised.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed a גר does not disqualify a woman through relations. רבי יהודה disagrees: he holds that a גר does. So the stronger shared feature also applies to the גר, and the common-feature proof stands for him.

keyTerms.meaning: Also, too.
He brings it, meaning he derives this law.
The 'common feature' method of proof, which learns a law from what two sources have in common.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה learns that the daughter of a גר is unfit for כהונה from the common feature of a חלל and a first-generation מצרי. This works because he holds a גר also disqualifies a woman through relations.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה: גֵּר נָמֵי פּוֹסֵל בְּבִיאָתוֹ,
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda holds: a convert also disqualifies a woman through his relations,

phrases.aramaic: וּמַיְיתֵי לַהּ בַּמָּה הַצַּד מֵהַאי דִּינָא.
phrases.english: and he derives it through a 'common feature' argument from this law.
phrases.notes: 'This law' means the cases of the חלל and the מצרי from the last step.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה: גֵּר נָמֵי פּוֹסֵל בְּבִיאָתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 28 by showing that רבי יהודה holds the גר shares the disputed feature.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the assumption behind the challenge, based on רבי יהודה's own position.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A גר does not disqualify a woman through relations, so he is unlike the חלל and the מצרי.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי יהודה a גר does disqualify through relations, so the common-feature proof holds.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, and רבי שמעון בן יוחי on a young גיורת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's view in the משנה. It then brings a ברייתא: רבי שמעון בן יוחי says a girl who converts before three years and a day is fit to marry a כהן, learned from the war with מדין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says about a convert... It was taught: רבי שמעון בן יוחי says: a female convert younger than three years and one day is fit for the priesthood. The verse says, 'And all the little ones among the women... keep alive for yourselves,' and פינחס the כהן was with them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new section by quoting רבי אליעזר בן יעקב from the משנה. It then brings a related ברייתא about a female convert marrying a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון בן יוחי reads the פסוק as allowing the soldiers to marry the young girls of מדין. פינחס, a כהן, was among those soldiers. So a girl who converts that young must be allowed even to a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא.
A female convert.
Fit to marry a כהן.
Little children.
פינחס, a כהן who went out to the war with מדין.

steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון בן יוחי is not saying every convert woman may marry a כהן. He allows only a girl who converted before age three years and one day.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר גֵּר.
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says: a convert...
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה, which says that if a גר marries a Jewish woman, their daughter is fit for כהונה.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai says:

phrases.aramaic: גִּיּוֹרֶת פְּחוּתָה מִבַּת שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד –
phrases.english: A female convert younger than three years and one day
is fit for the priesthood,
as it is said: 'And all the little ones among the women... keep alive for yourselves,'
phrases.notes: במדבר 31:18. He reads 'for yourselves' as 'you may marry them.'

phrases.english: and wasn't Pinchas with them!
phrases.notes: פינחס was a כהן, so this permission included a כהן too.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר גֵּר. תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The discussion of רבי יהודה's proof is finished. The גמרא moves on to the next opinion in the משנה and a related ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A girl who converts before three years and one day is fit to marry a כהן (רבי שמעון בן יוחי), learned from the girls of מדין, since פינחס was among the soldiers.

steps.title: How the רבנן read 'keep alive for yourselves'
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן disagree with רבי שמעון בן יוחי. They read 'keep alive for yourselves' as 'keep them as servants,' not as wives.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do the Rabbis read this verse? 'Keep alive for yourselves' means as male and female servants.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the רבנן deal with רבי שמעון בן יוחי's פסוק and gives their reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון בן יוחי's proof depends on reading 'for yourselves' as permission to marry. The רבנן read it as permission to keep the girls as servants. On that reading, the פסוק says nothing about marrying a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, here the ones who disagree with רבי שמעון בן יוחי.
Male and female servants.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis, how do they read this?
'Keep alive for yourselves' means as male and female servants.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן? הַחֲיוּ לָכֶם – לַעֲבָדִים וְלִשְׁפָחוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the רבנן avoid the proof that רבי שמעון בן יוחי brought in step 30.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Keep alive for yourselves' means you may marry them, even a כהן like פינחס.
steps.terutzMaskana: For the רבנן, 'for yourselves' means as servants, so there is no proof about marrying a כהן.

steps.title: All the views come from one פסוק about whom a כהן may marry
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב both build on the same פסוק in יחזקאל. רבי יהודה reads 'of the seed of Israel' as all of the seed. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב reads it as even part of the seed.
steps.simpleTranslation: They all learned from one verse: 'A widow and a divorcee they shall not take as wives, but only maidens of the seed of the house of Israel.' רבי יהודה holds: only if all the seed is from Israel. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב holds: 'of the seed' means even part of the seed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that all the תנאים in this argument draw their views from the same פסוק and read it differently. This step gives the readings of רבי יהודה and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, and the next step adds the rest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says a כהן marries women 'of the seed of the house of Israel.' רבי יהודה says the girl's whole lineage must be from Israel, so if one parent is a גר she is unfit. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב reads 'of the seed' as 'from part of the seed,' so one Jewish-born parent is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: They expounded one פסוק.
Holds, is of the opinion.
Seed, meaning lineage or descent.
Part of, some of.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה says a כהן may marry a woman only if all her lineage is from Israel, so the daughter of a גר is unfit. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says part of her lineage is enough, so if one parent was born Jewish she is fit. Both read 'מזרע בית ישראל' in יחזקאל.

phrases.english: And all of them expounded one verse:
'A widow and a divorcee they shall not take for themselves as wives,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אִם בְּתוּלֹת מִזֶּרַע בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל״,
phrases.english: but only maidens of the seed of the house of Israel,'
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 44:22, said about כהנים.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר: עַד דְּאִית כׇּל זֶרַע מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda holds: only if all of the seed is from Israel.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב סָבַר: ״מִזֶּרַע״, וַאֲפִילּוּ מִקְצָת זֶרַע.
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov holds: 'of the seed' means even part of the seed.
phrases.notes: He reads the letter מ in מזרע as 'some of,' so one parent born Jewish is enough.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכוּלָּן מִקְרָא אֶחָד דָּרְשׁוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Steps back from the details to show the single פסוק underneath the argument between רבי יהודה and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The argument over the daughter of a גר comes down to how to read 'מזרע בית ישראל': all of the lineage (רבי יהודה) or even part of it (רבי אליעזר בן יעקב).

steps.title: How רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון בן יוחי read the same verse
steps.stepSummary: The list of readings is finished. רבי יוסי reads 'of the seed of Israel' as anyone conceived in Israel. רבי שמעון בן יוחי reads it as a girl whose בתולים formed while she was Jewish.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי holds the verse means 'one who was conceived in Israel.' רבי שמעון בן יוחי holds it means 'one whose בתולים were formed in Israel.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the list it began in the last step. It shows that רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון בן יוחי also take their views from the same פסוק in יחזקאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי allows even the daughter of two converts to marry a כהן. Her parents were already Jewish when she was conceived, so she was 'seeded in Israel.' רבי שמעון בן יוחי allows a girl who converted before three years and a day. Her בתולים finished forming after she became Jewish, so for him she counts as 'virgins of the seed of Israel.'

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא in the משנה who allows the daughter of two converts to marry a כהן
Were 'seeded,' meaning conceived
Her signs of virginity, which finish forming at age three
Holds, is of the opinion

steps.whatToRemember: All four views (רבי יהודה, רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, רבי יוסי, רבי שמעון בן יוחי) come from one פסוק: 'בתולות מזרע בית ישראל' (יחזקאל 44:22). Each one reads 'the seed of Israel' differently.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון בן יוחי's case is not about who her parents were. He means a girl who converted herself while still very young. What matters to him is that she was Jewish by the time her בתולים formed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the whole מחלוקת in the משנה is one argument about how to read a single phrase in the פסוק.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei holds:
[the verse means] one who was conceived in Israel.
Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai holds:
[it means] one whose virginity was formed in Israel.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי סָבַר: מִי שֶׁנִּזְרְעוּ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the list from step 32 by adding the readings of רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון בן יוחי.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Every view in the משנה and the ברייתא comes from a different reading of 'מזרע בית ישראל'. The readings are: all of the seed (רבי יהודה), even part of the seed (רבי אליעזר בן יעקב), conceived in Israel (רבי יוסי), and בתולים formed in Israel (רבי שמעון בן יוחי).

steps.title: רב נחמן begins speaking to רבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces something רב נחמן said to רבא. What he said comes right after this line.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to רבא:
steps.whatsHappening: This is only an opening line. The גמרא is setting up a new conversation, and what רב נחמן actually says comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that the readings of the פסוק are finished, the גמרא moves to a new conversation between two אמוראים. This line only names who is speaking and to whom. The real content starts right after it.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who speaks first in this new exchange
The אמורא he is speaking to
Said to him

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said to Rava:

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן לְרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the list of readings is finished, the גמרא opens a new exchange between אמוראים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling yet. This line only introduces a statement by רב נחמן to רבא that comes next.
